_comment: Authored, reviewed, and posted VERBATIM. Grant does not compose these.
Every line must describe something a rep can actually do TODAY. Grant once told
a rep it would 'keep watching those states and flag new awards here' when no such
capability existed, and she never used it again — an announcement that oversells
is worse than none, because the first thing anyone tries is the thing promised.
Plain words, no code, no internal names. `capabilities` lists which unmet asks
this update closes; declaring those is what makes Grant follow up personally with

announcements.body:
Morning all — a few things I can do now that I couldn't last week.

*Campaigns.* I can build a Salesforce campaign and load leads onto it, and I'll always send you the link. Just say what you want on it.

*Email.* I can email you a list of leads directly — no more copying them out of Slack.

*Reminders.* Ask me to remind you about something and I'll actually come back to you. Say "stop reminding me" any time and I'll stop, no questions.

*Contacts.* If you tell me someone's name or number, I'll save it and note that it came from you. And I can pull contacts from ZoomInfo, including who not to call.

*Following up.* If something we started goes quiet, I'll check back in rather than letting it drop.

If you asked me for any of these before and I couldn't help — I'll come find you. Sorry for the wait.
